questions.text: Which scenario is an indirect prompt injection?

options.A: A user asks an ordinary question outside the assistant’s supported topic.
options.B: An attacker places instructions in a retrieved document to redirect the assistant.
options.C: The model returns malformed JSON despite a formatting instruction.
options.D: A rate limiter rejects a user who exceeds the request quota.

questions.explanation: Indirect injection delivers attacker instructions through external content processed as data, such as retrieved documents or emails.

questions.text: An input filter passes a normal account question, but the generated response includes an email address the user is not allowed to receive. Which design directly addresses both access and delivery?

options.A: Trust the output because the input filter already passed the question.
options.B: Add a system instruction and remove all output validation checks.
options.C: Increase the input length limit so the model has more room to explain.
options.D: Enforce authorization when retrieving data and check/redact sensitive output before delivery.

questions.explanation: Authorization limits what data can be accessed, while output checks provide another layer before delivery; input filtering alone cannot enforce either.

questions.text: detect_injection assigns encoding_evasion confidence=0.70 and returns passed=max_confidence < 0.75. If encoding_evasion is the only detection, what result follows?

options.A: passed=True with confidence=0.70, because the detection remains below the blocking threshold.
options.B: passed=False with confidence=0.70, because any detection automatically blocks.
options.C: passed=True with confidence=0.0, because passing clears the detection score.
options.D: passed=False with confidence=1.0, because encoding detections are always certain.

questions.explanation: The comparison 0.70 < 0.75 is True. The detection remains in the report but does not block at this threshold.
